note: None of the listed instruments can express the hedge thesis. The thesis depends on South African assets repricing on how the Johannesburg coalition turns out: the rand against the dollar, SA government bond yields and CDS spreads, and JSE banks and financials. No candidate on the list covers any of those assets or anything else about South African politics. Timing rules out the rest as well. The Johannesburg council vote comes after the November 4, 2026 election, but almost every market-price candidate settles in September or October 2026. That includes the Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, gold, silver and S&P 500 touch ladders for September, WTI for October, and the October central-bank decisions, so none of them can respond to the Johannesburg result. The only instruments that resolve later are elections in other countries: the US midterms, Brazil, Israel, Quebec, Toronto and others. None of them has a causal link to coalition bargaining in Johannesburg. Picking one would add unrelated risk rather than a hedge, so the answer is no instrument.
